# Objective

Study **BLSM 2013** and changes in **real household economic welfare** between IFLS4 (2007–08) and IFLS5 (2014–15).

The first estimand is the **ATT for actual recipients**, followed by ATT within *baseline-defined* subgroups. The primary outcome candidate is **real monthly household consumption per capita**. No causal estimates will be computed until treatment timing, household linkage, outcome construction and identification assumptions have been reviewed.

The scripts below use original Stata data and save **aggregate diagnostics only** to:

\`05_outputs/tables/blsm_2013/\`

\`\`\`{r setup, include=FALSE}
project_root <- if (file.exists("IFLS_Project.Rproj")) "." else ".."
knitr::opts_knit$set(root.dir=normalizePath(project_root,winslash="/"))
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo=TRUE,message=FALSE,warning=FALSE)
\`\`\`

## Step 1 — Verify BLSM program codes, receipt and timing

The IFLS5 Book 1 KSR1 questionnaire uses **KSR3TYPE column C = BLSM**, **KSR17 = receipt**, and KSR18/KSR22 as first/last dates for PKH/BLSM. It distinguishes BLT 2008 and PKH.

\`\`\`{r treatment-audit, eval=FALSE}
source("02_scripts/10_blsm_2013/01_treatment_audit.R")
\`\`\`

Read \`00_ksr1_variable_labels.csv\`, \`01_program_codes.csv\`, \`01_receipt_codes.csv\`, \`02_blsm_timing_classification.csv\`, and \`03_blsm_first_last_year.csv\`.

**Decisions:** Does the data label truly identify BLSM, and how many recipients first received it in 2013? Are there late/unknown dates? Do not treat missing records as control households. Inspect payment dates relative to the IFLS5 interview, and distinguish the 2013 program from assistance starting in late 2014.

## Step 2 — Inspect longitudinal linkage and household mobility

\`\`\`{r panel-audit, eval=FALSE}
source("02_scripts/10_blsm_2013/02_panel_audit.R")
\`\`\`

Review \`04_ptrack_linkage_counts.csv\`, \`05_splitoff_audit.csv\`, \`06_htrack_linkage_counts.csv\` and member/result-code frequencies. Use \`PIDLINK\` for tracking **people**; household-level analyses need an explicit policy for household splits and composition changes. Do not blindly merge \`HHID07 == HHID14\`.

**Decisions:** Do we use a stable-household panel, a 2007 baseline-household lineage, or an individual-anchored welfare panel? Estimate attrition/split-off sensitivity, and avoid defining inclusion through future outcomes of treatment.

## Step 3 — Audit KS consumption components for both waves

\`\`\`{r consumption-audit, eval=FALSE}
source("02_scripts/10_blsm_2013/03_welfare_inventory.R")
\`\`\`

Review \`09_welfare_file_inventory.csv\` and \`10_welfare_variable_dictionary.csv\`. In KS, weekly food, monthly nonfood, annual nonfood, education, housing, and own-produced/received food must be assigned to consistent categories and reference periods.

Candidate outcome: monthly consumption per capita, at **constant prices**. Document item recoding, missing/special codes, inclusions/exclusions, treatment-related spending, CPI and spatial deflation, number of current household members, and zero/implausible values. Do not sum KS variables until the full mapping is verified. A household cash transfer is not itself a consumption item.

## View audit outputs

Run each script from the Console once, then knit this notebook to display any completed tables.

\`\`\`{r audit-summary}
files <- c(
  "02_blsm_timing_classification.csv",
  "04_ptrack_linkage_counts.csv",
  "05_splitoff_audit.csv",
  "09_welfare_file_inventory.csv"
)
folder <- "05_outputs/tables/blsm_2013"
for (f in files) {
  file <- file.path(folder, f)
  cat("\n\n### ", f, "\n\n", sep="")
  if (file.exists(file)) {
    print(knitr::kable(utils::read.csv(file), caption=f))
  } else {
    cat("Not generated yet — run the corresponding script from the Console.\n")
  }
}
\`\`\`

## Step 4 — Audit interview dates and 2014 exposure contamination

Run the metadata scan below and inspect variable labels to determine precisely when IFLS5 interviews took place. This is particularly important when distinguishing 2013 BLSM from late-2014 payments.

```{r interview-timing-audit, eval=FALSE}
source("02_scripts/10_blsm_2013/04_interview_calendar_audit.R")
```

Review `11_interview_date_variable_candidates.csv`. Confirm exact day/month/year codes from the questionnaire before classifying treatment as pre-interview.

## Step 5 — Pretreatment covariates and heterogeneity audit (planned)

Candidate baseline \`X\`: real IFLS4 welfare and asset ownership, household size/composition, household-head education, employment, pre-existing cash assistance, urban/rural status, and region. Restrict to information known **before BLSM 2013**, and consider whether some IFLS4 reports are already affected by older BLT programs.

Prespecified subgroup ATT:
- Baseline poor versus vulnerable/nonpoor, using a documented 2007 welfare benchmark.
- Urban versus rural (IFLS4).
- Baseline household composition (e.g., with/without children).

**Avoid:** using 2014/15 poverty to define heterogeneity; it is post-treatment.

## Step 6 — Observational ATT identification (planned; no model yet)

Candidate design: doubly robust **panel DiD ATT** with baseline-covariate adjustment, conditional parallel trends, overlap, consistency, and no problematic spillovers. An ATT estimate is only credible if these assumptions are defensible. With two waves we cannot directly test pre-treatment parallel trends for welfare. Plan sensitivity to the 2013 fuel-price shock, program targeting, other assistance, attrition, measurement error, and inference that respects household clustering / survey design.

**No LATE without a valid instrument.** A KPS card or eligibility indicator cannot automatically be used as an IV; its assignment mechanism and exclusion restriction must be established.

## Step 7 — RAPSEM feasibility (future, separately identified)

RAPSEM estimates controlled direct and mediator effects, **not automatically ATT**. To apply it to observational BLSM receipt we would need:
- A validated treatment ignorability argument or an explicitly developed alternative;
- A *post-BLSM, pre-outcome* mediator, ideally measured with multiple valid latent indicators;
- A defensible treatment-by-baseline-covariate mediator interaction satisfying relevance and exclusion conditions;
- A theoretically and statistically justified adaptation of the G-estimation / factor-score correction and uncertainty quantification.

The IFLS4–IFLS5 pair by itself may not support a temporally separated post-treatment mediator and outcome. Do not invent a causal mediator from simultaneous IFLS5 measurements.
